results.quote: Six compartments, 1 at the bow through 6 at the stern.
Water counts in whole units, never below zero.
Inception marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Desinence marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Every pump starts LAMINAR. ... Water at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Emergency blow threshold, whole hull: 38. ... Keep one running overboard total from zero
Each cycle is five steps, in order, each finished in all six before the next.
Flood. Add the cycle's water. Don't stop at the volume; let it overfill.
Work bow to stern, 1 through 6. Anything above volume runs aft into the next compartment, leaving this one exactly full.
Since 1 goes before 2, one surge can carry down the whole line.
Whatever overtops 6 goes overboard.
LAMINAR at or above its inception mark goes CAVITATING.
CAVITATING only settles to LAMINAR at or below its desinence mark
in between, it holds. Log every change. (single pass per step; at-most-once is implied by one reading per cycle)
Size every discharge off current readings before touching a valve ... Then open them all together.
LAMINAR moves a quarter, CAVITATING half, rounded down. ... LAMINAR water goes overboard.
CAVITATING water backflows forward into the next compartment toward the bow; out of 1 it goes overboard.
Nobody watches volume here, so a compartment can sit overfull until next cycle's scuppers, and after cycle 5 it stays that way.
Sum all six. Strictly over 38: ... At 38 or under, leave it.
every compartment halves, rounded down, the difference overboard; note the cycle.

water in compartments 1 to 6, in order; the state of each pump (LAMINAR or CAVITATING); every state change as (cycle, compartment, before, after); the cycles in which a blow fired; the overboard tally; and a balance line: water at start plus everything flooded in, against water aboard plus overboard.
